run.question: We got a customer complaint about slow response times in Europe. The customer mentioned seeing request ID REQ-EU-8K4M2 in their error page. Find what happened with this request and which service had the issue.

report.summary: The complaint could not be tied to any service: the request identifier REQ-EU-8K4M2 does not appear in any source I could actually read, and the two sources that could have resolved it (Jaeger traces and Prometheus metrics) were unreachable for every call in this Run (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE). What I verified: the Elasticsearch target holds 1620 indices, all named app-185-geo-{region}-{service}-2024.01.NN (a different, geo-labelled application id) plus two system .ds- indices; those app-185 indices map @timestamp/level/message/region/response_time_ms/service but their documents lie outside the authorized window, so their content is unreadable here. Elasticsearch searches across all indices for the string REQ-EU-8K4M2 inside 2026-11-21T09:21:05Z–2026-11-22T09:21:05Z matched 0 documents, and pod-log greps for REQ-EU / REQ- in frontend, frontend-proxy, checkout and load-generator returned no lines (absence not proven). The only in-window anomalies I observed are (a) a cluster-wide container restart/DNS blip at 2026-11-22T08:04–08:05 (prometheus-server exit 255 at 08:04:13, prometheus-readonly-proxy nginx 'host not found in upstream prometheus:9090' and exit 1 at 08:04:42, ad/recommendation/currency telemetry-export UNAVAILABLE, and a single frontend gRPC 14 UNAVAILABLE / ECONNREFUSED to cart's ClusterIP 10.96.220.188:8080 at 08:05:00), and (b) an ongoing otel-collector failure to upload metrics to otel-collector:4318 (HTTP/2 preface error) from 09:16:37 to 09:20:57. All deployments report 1/1 ready with unchanged 2.0.2 images, no rollouts, no ingresses and no networkpolicies; flagd fault flags all default to 'off'. No root cause is named.

claims.text: The Elasticsearch target contains 1620 indices, all in six geo prefixes app-185-geo-{ap-northeast,ap-south,eu-central,eu-west,us-east,us-west} with 270 indices each; a slice of the index list shows entries such as app-185-geo-eu-west-cart-2024.01.01 with docs.count 1 and store.size about 8kb.

Apart from app-185-geo-* indices, the only other indices returned with expand_wildcards=all are .ds-.logs-deprecation.elasticsearch-default-2026.11.22-000001 and .ds-ilm-history-7-2026.11.22-000001; no otel-demo application log index was returned.
Index app-185-geo-eu-west-cart-2024.01.01 maps the fields @timestamp, level, message, region, response_time_ms and service.

The Deployment prometheus-readonly-proxy (nginx) failed to start at 2026-11-22T08:04:42: the previous container logged nginx: [emerg] host not found in upstream "prometheus:9090" in /etc/nginx/nginx.conf:22; the container's last termination was exit code 1 at 08:04:42, restartCount is 6, and it has been running again since 08:05:10.

The prometheus-server container in pod prometheus-9bc78b5f7-c9wx8 last terminated at 2026-11-22T08:04:13 with exit code 255 (reason Unknown) and restarted at 08:04:20; it is ready with restartCount 2.

The frontend container logged, at 2026-11-22T08:05:00.81Z, 'Error: 14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.220.188:8080' with stack frame .next/server/pages/api/cart.js, shortly after it started and reported 'Ready in 648ms' at 08:04:25; 10.96.220.188 is the ClusterIP of the cart Service.

Between 08:04:27 and 08:04:58 on 2026-11-22 several services failed to resolve or export telemetry: the ad pod logged java.net.UnknownHostException for flagd and otel-collector, the recommendation pod logged 'Transient error StatusCode.UNAVAILABLE encountered while exporting logs to otel-collector:4317', and the currency pod logged '[OTLP LOG GRPC Exporter] Export() failed: Deadline Exceeded'.

The otel-collector container logged repeated failures 'failed to upload metrics: reader collect and export timeout: rpc error: code = Unavailable ... error reading server preface: http2: failed reading the frame payload: http2: frame too large, note that the frame header looked like an HTTP/1.1 header' against {Addr: "10.96.247.55:4318", ServerName: "otel-collector:4318"} every 10 seconds from 2026-11-22T09:16:37 to 09:20:57.

All 21 otel-demo Deployments report availableReplicas 1, readyReplicas 1 and observedGeneration equal to generation; pods were created 2026-11-20T16:32:06Z–16:33:38Z with images ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-* (plus jaeger all-in-one 1.53.0, prometheus v3.5.0, nginx 1.28.0-alpine, flagd v0.12.8), i.e. no pod-template rollout inside the window, while container restartCount is 2 on most pods (kube-state-metrics 4, prometheus-readonly-proxy 6).

The flagd ConfigMap flagd-config holds demo.flagd.json in which every flag (productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, imageSlowLoad) has defaultVariant 'off'.

There are no Ingress objects and no NetworkPolicy objects in the cluster, and every one of the 26 Services in namespace otel-demo has a populated Endpoints subset (including cart at 10.244.0.4:8080 and prometheus at 10.244.0.11:9090).

The only application alerting rule in the prometheus ConfigMap is CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh, evaluated over traces_span_metrics_calls_total for k8s_namespace_name=otel-demo, service_name=checkout, span_kind SPAN_KIND_SERVER, span_name ~ .*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR over 50% for 2m; this is configuration, not an observed alert state.

Checkout logged successful PlaceOrder handling at 09:17:55, 09:18:39, 09:19:23 and 09:20:44 on 2026-11-22 with severity info messages '[PlaceOrder] user_id=..., user_currency=USD/CAD', 'payment went through (transaction_id: ...)' and 'order confirmation email sent'; no error-severity lines appear in its stdout for the window.

The cart Service was serving normal traffic later in the window: cart logged AddItemAsync/GetCartAsync/EmptyCartAsync calls with userId values up to 2026-11-22T09:20:44, and its Deployment reports 1/1 ready, so the single frontend ECONNREFUSED at 08:05:00 does not by itself show cart was broken during the complaint period.

Hypothesis that cart was the failing dependency behind the customer's error page was rejected as this cause: the only cart-related error is a single gRPC 14 UNAVAILABLE / ECONNREFUSED at 08:05:00, exactly when containers across the cluster were restarting after 08:04, and cart afterwards logged continuous successful cart operations and is 1/1 ready with populated endpoints.

The 08:04–08:05 failures are most consistent with a cluster-wide container restart and DNS-resolution blip (all pods show restartCount 2 with pods untouched since 2026-11-20, ad/recommendation/currency lost flagd, otel-collector and OTLP endpoints at 08:04:2x–08:04:5x, and the nginx proxy failed DNS for 'prometheus:9090'); the object that triggered it is not visible in the retained events, so this is a mechanism, not an established cause.

The otel-collector's continuous 'failed to upload metrics' errors to 10.96.247.55:4318 (HTTP/2 request answered by an HTTP/1.1 header) suggest a telemetry-pipeline misconfiguration on the collector's own OTLP HTTP endpoint; this could explain gaps or staleness in exported metrics but is not evidence of user-facing latency in any service.

Restore read access to the registered Jaeger and Prometheus targets (the in-cluster path goes through prometheus-readonly-proxy, whose nginx previously failed on upstream name 'prometheus:9090') and then query traces for trace-level request tags and rpc_*/http_server_request_duration_seconds_* series for a checkout/frontend latency comparison against a pre-window baseline before attributing the complaint to a service.

gaps: Jaeger was unreachable for every call in this Run (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE): traces_list_services, traces_list_operations, traces_search (frontend, frontend-proxy), traces_search_by_tags and traces_query_trace_by_id all failed, so no span, tag, duration or parent-child evidence about request REQ-EU-8K4M2 or about which operation was slow exists in this investigation.

Prometheus was unreachable for every call in this Run (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE): get_metric_names, get_prometheus_target, list_prometheus_rules, execute_prometheus_instant_query (up, time(), count(up), traces_span_metrics_calls_total) and metrics_range_query (traces_span_metrics_calls_total error rates) all failed, so traces_span_metrics_calls_total, rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_*, rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket, http_server_request_duration_seconds_count and kube_* series could not be read at all; missing series here are unknown, not zero.

The exact identifier REQ-EU-8K4M2 was not found: an Elasticsearch query_string search for "REQ-EU-8K4M2" across all 1620 indices inside 2026-11-21T09:21:05Z–2026-11-22T09:21:05Z returned total 0 (status no_data, 1620 shards successful), and pod-log greps for REQ-EU (frontend, checkout) and REQ- (frontend-proxy, load-generator) returned no lines; none of these results proves the request never existed, since logs are partial and Elasticsearch has no otel-demo index.

The geo-labelled Elasticsearch data is unreadable for this window: all 1620 app-185-geo-*-2024.01.NN indices carry a mapped @timestamp and their documents fall outside the authorized window (index names cover 2024.01.01–01.30 and the in-window search matched nothing), and the tool cannot disable the time filter, so the 'message', 'region' and 'response_time_ms' values of those documents remain unknown.

Nothing in the reachable evidence establishes why all containers restarted around 2026-11-22T08:04:13–08:05:10; the only in-window Kubernetes events are 4 events in namespace app-95 (Deployment ScalingReplicaSet, ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate, Pod Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started, Endpoints FailedToCreateEndpoint) and no event explains the otel-demo restarts or the DNS failures.

Whether the otel-collector 'failed to upload metrics' errors actually suppressed any of the metric series the complaint depends on could not be verified, because the collector's effective configuration (otel-collector ConfigMap key 'relay') and the Prometheus query path could not be exercised.

No customer-side or regional signal exists in the reachable data: nothing in the cluster, in pod logs or in the readable Elasticsearch metadata carries a Europe/geo dimension for otel-demo traffic, so the 'Europe' scope of the complaint is unverified.
next_steps: Verify connectivity of the registered Prometheus target (prometheus-readonly-proxy nginx upstream 'prometheus:9090', NodePort 9090) and of Jaeger (jaeger-query / jaeger-query-nodeport) so trace and latency evidence can be collected.

When Jaeger is reachable, search spans of frontend/frontend-proxy for request-identifier tags matching REQ-EU-8K4M2 and inspect the trace's checkout, currency, payment and shipping child spans for the slow operation.

When Prometheus is reachable, compare p95/p99 of rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket and traces_span_metrics_calls_total error ratios per service for the complaint period against an earlier baseline, starting with checkout (CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh rule) and frontend.
Identify the source that issues REQ-EU-… identifiers (frontend error page vs. an upstream gateway) so the ID can be correlated to a trace or log line.
Clarify with the application owner whether the folder of app-185-geo-* 2024 indices is a stale export rather than this incident's log store, since it is the only log-index family present.

content.alerting:
groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
